read: As of November 24, 2026, 5 of 10 fingerprint states are active: vol shock (since November 20, 2026); vol inversion (since November 17, 2026); risk-off / risk-on rotation (since October 16, 2026); broadening / narrowing (since October 20, 2026); energy shock (since November 16, 2026).
Equities are down 6.1% over 21 sessions while HY OAS has widened 42 bp — inside the deliberately unclassified 25–50 bp band: credit is leaning, not confirming.
Financial conditions still print loose: the NFCI is -0.44, below the zero line that marks average tightness.
Gold is falling with equities (-11.5% over 21 sessions), so the haven bid is not in gold on these definitions.
Rotation patterns active: Defensive rotation, Concentration unwind.

board.title: Vol shock
board.definition: max(VIX close, trailing 5 sessions) ≥ 30 AND VIX 21 sessions ago < 25 — a spike out of a calm regime, not a chronic high.

board.title: Vol inversion
board.definition: VIXCLS − VXVCLS > 0: spot vol above 3-month vol (backwardation).

board.title: Risk-off / risk-on rotation
board.definition: Mean 21-session return of XLP, XLU, XLV minus mean of XLY, XLI, XLK ≥ +3.0 pp → risk-off rotation; ≤ −3.0 pp → risk-on rotation (mirror).

board.title: Broadening / narrowing
board.definition: R21(RSP) − R21(SPY) ≥ +1.5 pp → broadening; ≤ −1.5 pp → narrowing. RSP is the equal-weight index — the average stock — so the spread is the breadth proxy (labelled a proxy: true constituent breadth has no free source).

board.title: Credit-confirmed stress / equity-only divergence
board.definition: R21(SPY) ≤ −5% AND HY OAS 21-session widening ≥ +0.50 → credit-confirmed stress. The same equity leg with widening < +0.25 → equity-only divergence. The band between is deliberately unclassified; the measured widening is shown either way.

board.title: Haven bid
board.definition: R21(GLD) > 0 AND R21(SPY) < 0 AND C21(broad dollar) > 0. Its failure during an equity fall is informative and is reported as such.

board.title: Rates shock
board.definition: |C21(10-year Treasury yield)| ≥ 0.40 (40 bp in 21 sessions), direction labelled.

board.title: Energy shock
board.definition: |R21(WTI crude)| ≥ 15%, direction labelled. (WTI is a FRED series with a publication lag of about a week; the window is 21 of its own observations.)

board.title: Conditions tightening
board.definition: NFCI 13-week change ≥ +0.10 while the NFCI level is still below 0 — conditions moving the wrong way from a loose base, weeks before any stress index prints positive. Evaluated on weekly closes.

board.title: Snapback (inflection candidate)
board.definition: R21(SPY) ≤ −5% AND R5(SPY) ≥ +3%: a violent reversal off a drawdown. Labelled the weakest signal of the set — most snapbacks fail; the state exists so the board can say one is being attempted.

inflections.title: Vol-curve flip
inflections.definition: VIXCLS − VXVCLS crosses zero. Up-cross = inversion onset (stress arriving); down-cross = normalisation (the earliest standard sign a dislocation is ending).

inflections.title: Spread peak / deterioration turn
inflections.definition: HY OAS prints a 63-session high, then tightens ≥ 0.15 from that high within 21 sessions → credit has turned. Mirror: a 63-session low followed by ≥ 0.15 of widening within 21 sessions is the deterioration inflection.

inflections.title: Momentum zero-cross
inflections.definition: The S&P 500's trailing 21-session return (SPY) crosses zero in either direction; the board dates the current momentum regime.

inflections.title: Sector breadth thrust
inflections.definition: The share of the 15 grid panels in positive 21-session momentum moves from ≤ 30% to ≥ 70% within the band (thrust up), or the reverse (thrust down). Computed entirely from the section's own grid — no external breadth data.

inflections.title: Curve re-steepening
inflections.definition: C21(T10Y2Y) ≥ +0.15 after a trailing 63-session minimum ≤ 0 — the post-inversion turn that historically sits much closer to recessions than the inversion itself.

inflections.title: Dollar turn
inflections.definition: Sign flip of C21(broad dollar) after at least 42 sessions of the opposite sign — a dollar momentum regime change.

patterns.title: Defensive rotation
patterns.definition: Risk-off rotation active AND at least two of XLP/XLU/XLV in Leading while XLK is in Lagging.

patterns.title: Cyclical rotation (risk-on)
patterns.definition: Risk-on rotation active AND at least two of XLY/XLI/XLK in Leading while XLP is in Lagging (the mirror of defensive rotation).

patterns.title: Concentration unwind
patterns.definition: Broadening active AND QQQ or XLK in Lagging AND RSP in Leading or Improving: leadership leaving the mega-caps without leaving equities.

patterns.title: Broad liquidation
patterns.definition: At least 12 of the 15 grid panels with negative 21-session momentum AND credit-confirmed stress active: everything falling together, credit included.

segments.title: Leading indicators
segments.subtitle: The series that historically turn before broad risk — credit, financial conditions, the volatility term structure, the curve, and the fastest hard data. Each panel is captioned with the lead it is there to capture.

indicators.title: High-yield credit spread (OAS)
indicators.why: Credit spreads typically widen before equity drawdowns deepen and tighten before durable equity bottoms; this is the confirmation channel for any equity stress. The same series is carried by the Market Pulse layer; it is archived here as well because the fingerprint states are computed only from this section's own archive.
indicators.source: FRED: BAMLH0A0HYM2 — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/BAMLH0A0HYM2
indicators.definition: ICE BofA US High Yield Index option-adjusted spread (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2); daily, in percent.
indicators.note: Widely used as the credit-confirmation gauge: the fingerprint bar is +0.50 of widening over 21 sessions.

indicators.title: Investment-grade credit spread (OAS)
indicators.why: Slower, higher-quality credit. IG widening after HY-only widening marks stress graduating up the quality ladder; IG staying calm while HY widens marks a contained, low-quality event.
indicators.source: FRED: BAMLC0A0CM — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/BAMLC0A0CM
indicators.definition: ICE BofA US Corporate Index option-adjusted spread (FRED BAMLC0A0CM); daily, in percent.

indicators.title: Excess bond premium
indicators.why: The Gilchrist–Zakrajšek credit-sentiment component of corporate spreads: the part of spreads not explained by expected default. It rises ahead of recessions and equity bear markets in the Fed's own work, and led the 2007–08 widening. Read by the existing pulse fetcher from the same FEDS Notes file.
indicators.source: Federal Reserve FEDS Notes EBP series — federalreserve.gov
indicators.definition: Excess Bond Premium (Gilchrist–Zakrajšek methodology, FEDS Notes series) — the non-default component of corporate bond spreads; monthly, in percentage points.
indicators.note: Monthly and revised with the FEDS vintage; a sentiment gauge, not a traded price.

indicators.title: Chicago Fed NFCI
indicators.why: Composite financial conditions lead real activity and risk-asset stress by construction of the Chicago Fed's factor model (105 weekly series). Positive = tighter than average. The level is the section's conditions anchor: markets can fall a long way while this still prints loose, and that gap is a classification signal.
indicators.source: FRED: NFCI — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/NFCI
indicators.definition: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index (FRED NFCI); weekly (week ended Wednesday, published Friday), index (0 = average conditions).
indicators.note: Restated by the Chicago Fed as source data revise; the archive keeps the latest vintage.

indicators.title: NFCI — credit subindex
indicators.why: The credit component of the NFCI: credit reprices fast *during* events, so this subindex is the coincident-to-early read on whether a market move is becoming a funding problem.
indicators.source: FRED: NFCICREDIT — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/NFCICREDIT
indicators.definition: Chicago Fed NFCI credit subindex (FRED NFCICREDIT); weekly, index (0 = average).

indicators.title: NFCI — leverage subindex
indicators.why: The leverage component of the NFCI: leverage builds slowly *before* events, so a rising leverage subindex from a low base is the quiet vulnerability signal — the mirror image of the credit subindex's fast repricing.
indicators.source: FRED: NFCILEVERAGE — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/NFCILEVERAGE
indicators.definition: Chicago Fed NFCI leverage subindex (FRED NFCILEVERAGE); weekly, index (0 = average).

indicators.title: NFCI — risk subindex
indicators.why: The risk component of the NFCI (volatility and risk-appetite measures): the fastest-moving of the three subindexes, and the one that should move first if a vol event is becoming a conditions event.
indicators.source: FRED: NFCIRISK — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/NFCIRISK
indicators.definition: Chicago Fed NFCI risk subindex (FRED NFCIRISK); weekly, index (0 = average).

indicators.title: Chicago Fed ANFCI (adjusted)
indicators.why: The NFCI adjusted to remove the part of conditions explained by the state of the economy itself — the purer financial impulse. Agreement between NFCI and ANFCI is a robustness check on the conditions read.
indicators.source: FRED: ANFCI — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/ANFCI
indicators.definition: Chicago Fed Adjusted NFCI (FRED ANFCI); weekly, index (0 = average conditions).

indicators.title: St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index
indicators.why: A second conditions composite, built differently (18 weekly rates, spreads and vol series, principal components). Agreement between STLFSI4 and the NFCI family is the robustness check; divergence is itself information about which construction is driving the read.
indicators.source: FRED: STLFSI4 — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/STLFSI4
indicators.definition: St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index, version 4 (FRED STLFSI4); weekly, index (0 = average stress).

indicators.title: VIX (spot)
indicators.why: The 30-day implied volatility of the S&P 500. Spot vol is coincident, but its level against the 3-month VIX (the derived spread below) is one of the cleanest stress fingerprints in free data.
indicators.source: FRED: VIXCLS — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/VIXCLS
indicators.definition: CBOE Volatility Index, daily close (FRED VIXCLS); daily, in vol points.

indicators.title: VIX 3-month (VXV)
indicators.why: The 3-month implied volatility of the S&P 500 — the denominator of the vol term structure. Spot above 3-month (backwardation) marks dislocation onset; normalisation has historically been among the earliest signs a dislocation is ending.
indicators.source: FRED: VXVCLS — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/VXVCLS
indicators.definition: CBOE VIX 3-Month Volatility Index, daily close (FRED VXVCLS); daily, in vol points.

indicators.title: Gold vol (GVZ)
indicators.why: Implied volatility of gold. A companion to the equity vol panel: gold vol rising with equity vol marks a broad haven scramble; gold vol calm while equity vol spikes marks an equity-local event.
indicators.source: FRED: GVZCLS — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GVZCLS
indicators.definition: CBOE Gold ETF Volatility Index, daily close (FRED GVZCLS); daily, in vol points.

indicators.title: Oil vol (OVX)
indicators.why: Implied volatility of crude oil. The companion gauge for energy shocks: an oil price move with OVX spiking is a supply-scare signature; the same move with OVX falling is an unwind.
indicators.source: FRED: OVXCLS — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/OVXCLS
indicators.definition: CBOE Crude Oil ETF Volatility Index, daily close (FRED OVXCLS); daily, in vol points.

indicators.title: Yield curve, 10y − 2y
indicators.why: The classic slow lead: inversion precedes recessions by quarters. The nearer-term signal this series contributes is the inflection — re-steepening after inversion has historically sat much closer to recessions than the inversion itself (Section 4 of the methodology).
indicators.source: FRED: T10Y2Y — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/T10Y2Y
indicators.definition: 10-year Treasury yield minus 2-year Treasury yield (FRED T10Y2Y); daily, in percentage points.

indicators.title: Yield curve, 10y − 3m
indicators.why: The 10y−3m slope — the curve measure in the New York Fed's recession-probability model. Shown beside 10y−2y because the two can disagree when the front end is pinned by the expected policy path.
indicators.source: FRED: T10Y3M — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/T10Y3M
indicators.definition: 10-year Treasury yield minus 3-month Treasury yield (FRED T10Y3M); daily, in percentage points.

indicators.title: Initial jobless claims
indicators.why: The fastest hard-data labour series (weekly, one-week lag). A sustained turn up in claims is the standard early recession tell; claims staying low while markets fall is itself a classification signal — a financial event, not yet a macro event.
indicators.source: FRED: ICSA — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/ICSA
indicators.definition: Initial claims for unemployment insurance, seasonally adjusted (FRED ICSA); weekly, in persons.

indicators.title: Consumer sentiment (Michigan)
indicators.why: Household expectations turn early but noisily. Included as context and weighted accordingly: monthly, survey-based, and prone to partisan swings that do not map to spending.
indicators.source: FRED: UMCSENT — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UMCSENT
indicators.definition: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment index (FRED UMCSENT); monthly, index (1966 = 100).
indicators.note: Labelled monthly and noisy on the page, per the design: context, not a trigger.

indicators.why: The breadth proxy: the average stock, as opposed to the cap-weighted index. RSP minus SPY momentum is the broadening/narrowing fingerprint — true constituent breadth has no free source, so the proxy is labelled as one.

segments.title: Cross-asset
segments.subtitle: Index levels, yields, the dollar, energy, gold, Bitcoin, and credit ETF prices — the raw material of the movers table.

indicators.title: S&P 500 index
indicators.why: The index level itself (FRED's daily S&P 500), shown beside the SPY ETF so index and traded price can be compared; the movers table's equity anchor.

indicators.definition: S&P 500 index level (FRED SP500); daily, in index points.

indicators.title: Nasdaq Composite
indicators.why: The broader growth tape. Nasdaq's one-day snaps in a drawdown are the raw material the snapback state tests at the 5-session window.
indicators.source: FRED: NASDAQCOM — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/NASDAQCOM
indicators.definition: Nasdaq Composite index level (FRED NASDAQCOM); daily, in index points.

indicators.title: 2-year Treasury yield
indicators.why: The policy-expectations yield. Its 21-session change separates a market fall the Fed is expected to answer from one it is expected to watch.
indicators.source: FRED: DGS2 — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2
indicators.definition: 2-year Treasury constant maturity rate (FRED DGS2); daily, in percent.

indicators.title: 10-year Treasury yield
indicators.why: The long rate. A 21-session move of 40 bp or more, either way, is the rates-shock fingerprint — the direction decides whether it is a growth scare or an inflation scare.
indicators.source: FRED: DGS10 — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10
indicators.definition: 10-year Treasury constant maturity rate (FRED DGS10); daily, in percent.

indicators.title: 10-year breakeven inflation
indicators.why: The market's 10-year inflation expectation, priced daily: separates an inflation scare the market believes from one it expects policy to crush.
indicators.source: FRED: T10YIE — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/T10YIE
indicators.definition: 10-year breakeven inflation rate (FRED T10YIE); daily, in percent.

indicators.title: 10-year real yield (TIPS)
indicators.why: The real long rate — the tightness of financial conditions that does not depend on inflation expectations. Rising real yields into an equity fall mark a policy-driven event.
indicators.source: FRED: DFII10 — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DFII10
indicators.definition: 10-year Treasury inflation-indexed constant maturity rate (FRED DFII10); daily, in percent.

indicators.title: Broad dollar index
indicators.why: A rising dollar tightens global financial conditions with a lag; dollar momentum turns have led risk turns in tightening cycles. The dollar-turn inflection (Section 4 of the methodology) is computed from this series. Publication lags the observation by several days.
indicators.source: FRED: DTWEXBGS — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DTWEXBGS
indicators.definition: Nominal broad US dollar index (FRED DTWEXBGS); daily, index (Jan 2006 = 100).
indicators.note: Publication lag: the latest print is several business days old at any build.

indicators.title: Euro (USD per EUR)
indicators.why: The bilateral leg of the dollar read and the spot rate behind the pulse layer's cross-currency basis: a euro falling with the broad dollar rising confirms a dollar event rather than a euro event.
indicators.source: FRED: DEXUSEU — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DEXUSEU
indicators.definition: US dollar to one euro exchange rate (FRED DEXUSEU); daily, in USD per EUR.

indicators.title: WTI crude
indicators.why: The energy-shock leg: a 21-session move of 15% or more, either direction, is a fingerprint — up is a supply shock, down is the shock unwinding or demand failing, and the two have opposite inflation implications. Publication lags by about a week.
indicators.source: FRED: DCOILWTICO — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILWTICO
indicators.definition: Crude oil price, West Texas Intermediate (FRED DCOILWTICO); daily, in USD per barrel.
indicators.note: Publication lag: the latest print is about a week old at any build.

indicators.title: Brent crude
indicators.why: The global crude benchmark, beside WTI: the Brent–WTI gap separates a global supply event from a US logistics event.
indicators.source: FRED: DCOILBRENTEU — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILBRENTEU
indicators.definition: Crude oil price, Brent Europe (FRED DCOILBRENTEU); daily, in USD per barrel.
indicators.note: Publication lag: the latest print is about a week old at any build.

indicators.title: Bitcoin
indicators.why: The most liquid 24/7 risk asset: it trades through weekends and holidays when nothing else on the page does, so its weekend moves are the first print of the next session's risk appetite.
indicators.source: FRED: CBBTCUSD — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CBBTCUSD
indicators.definition: Coinbase Bitcoin price (FRED CBBTCUSD); daily, in USD.

indicators.title: High-yield bonds (HYG)
indicators.why: The traded price of high-yield credit — the equity market's own credit gauge, beside the OAS. Price and spread disagreeing is a flow signal, not a data error.
indicators.source: Yahoo Finance chart API: HYG — finance.yahoo.com/quote/HYG
indicators.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: HYG (unadjusted close)
indicators.definition: Daily unadjusted close of iShares iBoxx $ High Yield Corporate Bond ETF (HYG), in USD; trading days only.

indicators.title: Investment-grade bonds (LQD)
indicators.why: The traded price of investment-grade credit — see HYG.
indicators.source: Yahoo Finance chart API: LQD — finance.yahoo.com/quote/LQD
indicators.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: LQD (unadjusted close)
indicators.definition: Daily unadjusted close of iShares iBoxx $ Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF (LQD), in USD; trading days only.

indicators.title: Long Treasuries (TLT)
indicators.why: Duration as an asset: when equities fall and TLT rises, duration is doing the haven work; when both fall, the shock is in rates themselves.
indicators.source: Yahoo Finance chart API: TLT — finance.yahoo.com/quote/TLT
indicators.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: TLT (unadjusted close)
indicators.definition: Daily unadjusted close of iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT), in USD; trading days only.

indicators.title: Gold (GLD)
indicators.why: Gold. FRED's spot fixing series were retired by their source, so the free route is the ETF. The haven-bid fingerprint needs gold *up* while equities fall — gold falling with equities is reported as a failed haven, which is itself the signal.
indicators.source: Yahoo Finance chart API: GLD — finance.yahoo.com/quote/GLD
indicators.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: GLD (unadjusted close)
indicators.definition: Daily unadjusted close of SPDR Gold Shares (GLD), in USD; trading days only.
indicators.note: FRED retired both LBMA fixing series (GOLDAMGBD228NLBM / GOLDPMGBD228NLBM); the ETF is the free source.

indicators.title: Oil fund (USO)
indicators.why: The traded oil price, beside the FRED spot prints: USO trades daily with no publication lag, so it is the freshest energy read on the page (futures-based, so it carries roll yield).
indicators.source: Yahoo Finance chart API: USO — finance.yahoo.com/quote/USO
indicators.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: USO (unadjusted close)
indicators.definition: Daily unadjusted close of United States Oil Fund (USO), in USD; trading days only.

segments.title: Derived spreads
segments.subtitle: Computed by this build from the archived series above; the construction is stated in each definition. No inputs beyond this section's own archive.

indicators.title: Volatility term structure (VIX − VXV)
indicators.why: Spot vol above 3-month vol (backwardation) is a coincident-to-slightly-leading stress marker: it flips at the onset of dislocations, and its normalisation has historically been one of the earliest signs a dislocation is ending. This spread is the vol-inversion fingerprint and the vol-curve-flip inflection.
indicators.source: Computed by this build from FRED VIXCLS and VXVCLS, archived in this section — github.com/fcela/frb-heat-index (data/momentum)
indicators.definition: CBOE Volatility Index minus CBOE VIX 3-Month Volatility Index, on dates both are observed (FRED VIXCLS, VXVCLS); daily, in vol points. Positive = backwardation (inversion).

indicators.title: Defensive-minus-cyclical momentum spread
indicators.why: The measured value behind the risk-off / risk-on rotation fingerprint, as a line: the 21-session return of the defensive trio (staples, utilities, health care) minus the cyclical trio (discretionary, industrials, technology). Sustained readings beyond ±3 pp are a rotation regime, not a day of noise.
indicators.source: Computed by this build from the archived sector closes in this section — github.com/fcela/frb-heat-index (data/momentum)
indicators.definition: Mean trailing 21-session return of XLP, XLU, XLV minus mean trailing 21-session return of XLY, XLI, XLK, on their common trading days; daily, in percentage points.
